context.clinical_context_summary: 69-year-old female with a past medical history of acute kidney failure (including acute cortical necrosis), rhabdomyolysis, and prior bacteremia on no home medications. Presents with fall. Key risks: high risk for recurrent acute kidney injury with dehydration/contrast exposure/nephrotoxins; possible frailty and fall-related injury (head trauma, fracture) and rhabdomyolysis after prolonged down time; prior bacteremia raises concern for occult infection if febrile or hypotensive. Baseline vitals appear generally stable with occasional low SpO2 (nadir 86%) and an unusually low temperature distribution (34.9–35.1°C) suggesting peripheral/axillary measurement or device bias; interpret hypothermia/fever thresholds accordingly.
context.rationale: Normal ranges were centered on the patient’s observed baselines (HR mean ~69, SBP mean ~117, RR mean ~16) with conservative buffers given age and fall risk. BP and HR warning limits reflect standard geriatric safety cutoffs for brady/tachycardia and hypotension/hypertension in the absence of rate-limiting or antihypertensive medications. SpO2 normal set to ≥95% since baseline is high, but warning low set at 92% because there are prior dips to 86% and any recurrent desaturation after a fall warrants evaluation. Temperature readings are consistently ~35.0°C, strongly suggesting axillary/peripheral technique or device offset; thresholds were adjusted to this apparent baseline, but any rise above this range could still represent fever relative to baseline and should prompt infection workup, especially given prior bacteremia.
